chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woad (a dyeing plant), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it for the old man, the aged'.

key_terms.الْوَسْمَةِ: Woad, a plant used as a dye for hair
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا: There is no problem with it / It is permissible
key_terms.لِلشَّيْخِ الْكَبِيرِ: For the old man / the aged

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for men to use woad to dye their hair black according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits the use of woad (*kattam*) for elderly men, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that dyeing hair is permissible to distinguish men from women or to counter the effects of aging, provided it does not involve deception. This ruling is often contextualized within the broader tradition of the Prophet and Imams using henna and kattam to remove the 'grayness' of old age, emphasizing natural appearance over artificial alteration. The specific mention of 'al-shaykh al-kabir' highlights the concession for those seeking to appear more vigorous or distinguished in their community.
